ox.text: A pumpkin is a fruit, not a vegetable.
ox.explanation: It grows from a flower and holds seeds, so it's a fruit. Pie agrees.

ox.text: Black cats are thought to be bad luck everywhere in the world.
ox.explanation: Nope! In Britain and Japan, black cats are often good luck.

ox.text: Vampire bats share their dinner with hungry roommates.
ox.explanation: True! They share meals with roommates who missed dinner. Spooky, but sweet.

buzzers.text: Which monster wears bandages from head to toe?
What box does a vampire nap in all day long?
What do kids shout when you open the door on Halloween night?

final.text: What do you call a group of owls?
final.explanation: A parliament of owls. Very wise, very serious, mostly asleep.

ox.text: An owl can turn its head all the way around, a full 360 degrees.
ox.explanation: Close! Owls manage about 270 degrees. Still a great party trick.

ox.text: In the original 1897 novel, Count Dracula can't go outside in daylight.
ox.explanation: He strolls around London by day. He's just weaker in the sun.

ox.text: Babies are born with more bones than grown-ups have.
ox.explanation: Babies have about 300. Many fuse together, so adults end up with 206.

buzzers.text: How many legs does a spider have?
In the old stories, what turns a person into a werewolf?
Which spooky someone is all bones and no body?

final.text: Before pumpkins, what did people in Ireland carve into spooky lanterns?
final.explanation: Turnips! In America, pumpkins were bigger and far easier to carve.

tracks.text: What's the title of this piece?
clues: The fiddler tunes one string wrong on purpose, for extra spookiness.
It's French, and a harp chimes twelve times for midnight at the start.

tracks.text: What's the title of this piece?
tracks.answer: In the Hall of the Mountain King
aliases: In the Hall of the Mountain King
The Hall of the Mountain King
tracks.explanation: In the Hall of the Mountain King
clues: It starts sneaky-quiet and keeps getting faster and louder.
It's from a Norwegian play, and grumpy trolls are chasing someone.

credit.title: In the Hall of the Mountain King (Peer Gynt Suite No. 1, Op. 46)
credit.author: Edvard Grieg

tracks.text: What's the title of this piece?
tracks.answer: Toccata and Fugue in D minor
aliases: Toccata and Fugue in D minor
tracks.explanation: Toccata and Fugue in D minor
clues: It's played on one enormous instrument with lots of pipes.
It's German and Baroque, and it opens with a dramatic twirl and a huge rumbling chord.

credit.title: Toccata and Fugue in D minor, BWV 565
credit.author: Johann Sebastian Bach
credit.performer: Wikipedia user "Cor anglais 16" (Flentrop organ, Oberlin Conservatory)
